summary: Adds an optional LINK_CUSTOM_ALPHABET setting that controls which characters random short-link codes are made from (default = the same alphabet as before), and lets user-chosen custom addresses also use characters from that alphabet.

statements.why: No login/data/money change; default alphabet equals the old hard-coded one (server/env.js, utils.js:14), so behaviour is unchanged unless the owner sets it.
True, documents the new optional setting.

statements.text: The agent also changed server/env.js, server/handlers/validators.handler.js and server/utils/utils.js, in ways plain can't describe yet.
Add LINK_CUSTOM_ALPHABET to your hosting settings (like Vercel). It's also missing from .env.example.
statements.why: The setting is optional with a default identical to the old behaviour (env.js str({default: ...}), and empty values are dropped), so nothing needs adding. It is not missing: this commit adds it to .example.env (the repo's example file name).

misses.what: The owner can now choose which characters random short-link codes use via LINK_CUSTOM_ALPHABET; leaving it unset keeps today's codes exactly the same.
If the alphabet is customised, users' own custom link addresses are also allowed to contain those extra characters (validators.handler.js:48,123).
